text: Counsel for appellants in a mortgage-foreclosure appeal filed an amended initial brief and a reply brief containing forty-six defective citations to case law: thirty-one in the amended initial brief and fifteen in the reply, including one wholly fabricated case and multiple real cases cited for propositions they do not support. Counsel admitted using AI as a research tool without independently verifying the citations it produced. The court found generative AI was not merely his "supplemental research tool" but his "primary or only one."
asserted_by: asserting party not identified in the indexed source fields
ai_system_name: Unnamed generative AI (admitted by counsel; court finding)
deployer: Kenneth H. Keefe, The Keefe Law Firm, P.A., South Pasadena, Florida, counsel for appellants
canonical_source_conflicted: Forty-six fabricated or misrepresented case citations, including the wholly fictitious Board of Regents v. Wilson, 365 So. 2d 213 (Fla. 1st DCA 1979), against the appellate rules of professional candor
mitigation_gap: Counsel used generative AI "without any apparent guardrails," per the court's finding, and did not independently verify any of the AI-generated authorities through reliable legal research sources before filing.
reliance_or_harm: The court struck the amended initial and reply briefs, fined counsel $1,500 ($500 for a belated show-cause response plus $1,000 for the AI misuse) payable to the clerk within 14 days, made counsel personally liable for the opposing party's appellate attorney's fees for researching and responding to the defective briefs (amount remanded to the trial court to determine), referred counsel to The Florida Bar, and expressly barred him from charging his clients for either the fine or the fee award. The underlying judgment was affirmed on the merits based on later, corrected briefing.
source_locator: Capital Standard, LLC v. U.S. Bank National Association, as trustee for Bear Stearns Asset Backed Securities I Trust 2005-AC9, No. 2D2024-1392 (Fla. 2d DCA)
